notes: No accepted C++ was collected (three WA, two RTE), so orig.cpp is the official CEOI 2022 solution (the accepted submission in the CEOI 2022 Kattis package). Any non-crossing drawing is accepted, so checker.py checks the permutation and runs a Shamos-Hoey sweep for crossing edges. On 300 random cases (reference output, the same with two labels swapped, a random permutation) it agreed with an independent all-pairs segment test every time, and the reference passed on every case, the samples and --max. The official CEOI output validator (output_validators/validator/validate.cpp) is not used: it misses crossings. Its sweep keeps active segments in a multiset ordered by left-endpoint y instead of by height at the sweep line, and rechecks no neighbours when a segment ends, so it compares a new segment with just one or two others. On 600 random permutations of gen.py cases (N <= 42) it accepted 16 that have a real crossing, and checker.py and the all-pairs test rejected all 16. No case went the other way: it rejected nothing that checker.py accepts, and it accepted the reference on 900 gen.py cases. Smallest such case: N = 4, edges 1-2 1-3 3-4, points (19870 394816900) (6146 37773316) (31300 979690000) (4295 18447025), output 2 4 3 1. Edge 1-2 (point 4 to point 1) crosses edge 3-4 (point 3 to point 2), but the validator never compares those two.
